column1: # tuning.tsv - THE TIMING AND LEVEL OF EVERY PART OF EVERY SOUND, and how loud each cue sits.
# The one owner of these numbers: soundgen reads it at build time and nothing else holds them.
# Edit it by hand, or by ear with the tuner on /sounds (`npm run tune`, docs/AUDIO.md "How to tune").
# Columns are separated by TABS; # starts a comment.
# THE STOCK SET DOWN (flip deck) has no time of its own: it is heard when the stock held in the air comes down,
# ANIM_DECK_DOWN_MS after the trump lands (c/src/anim_plan.h), whatever its time column says.
# PART lines: one part of one cue's gesture (a grab, a thumb slide, a landing).
#   <cue>, <role>    the take it is in: the cue as RECIPES in soundgen.c names it, and main, tight or prelude
#   <at ms>          where the part sits from the cue's moment, negative before it (its peak, its onset for a
#                    stroke, a slide or a soft lift or placement); for strokes, where the scrape is first heard (0: as the cards start moving)
#   <at spread ms>   drawn up to this much earlier, a take at a time (0: always at <at ms>)
#   <dB>             its level on the deal's scale, before the common gain (by peak, or by loudest 50 ms RMS
#                    for the discard's parts, the strokes and the slide into the hand), the loudest it is drawn
#   <dB spread>      drawn up to this much quieter, a take at a time (0: always at <dB>)
# The common gain then lifts every card take together, so the loudest peaks at -3 dBFS (soundgen.c PEAK_DB):
# raising the loudest part lowers everything else, and the balance is what these numbers say.
# Levels from the games' own (*_game.py) and the levels study of 2026-11-07 (docs/AUDIO.md "The balance between
# the parts": a landing ~25 dB over the grab and slide before it, the discard videos shot twice as far away).

column9: deal, opening a run: thumb slide
deal, opening a run: grab off the stock
deal: card lands on the cloth
trump: deck set down on it
lift, opening a run: two-finger grab
lift, opening a run: thumb slide
attack: card lands on the table
cover: card lands on a card
transfer: shfff to the next defender
bout end: strokes gathering the table

column1: # MIX lines: how loud each cue sits against the others, for every host (soundgen writes them into the take table
#   <gain>       against the level its files were written at: 1000 for every model (the parts above set them)
#   <pitch>      how far a play's speed may wander either way (60 is about a semitone); 0 for every model
#   <level>      how far its level may wander either way
#   <per card>   louder by this for each card past the first, up to +600
# The placeholders' gains (Alex 2026-11-07: "turn them down") by loudest 50 ms RMS: the game over -26 (just under
# a card landing at about -22), a seat going out -30, a good -34 and the hand-off -38 (heard every bout).
# Their files' own loudest 50 ms RMS, which the gains bring there: out -6.6, good -6.8, hand-off -11.4, finish -5.9,
# fool -5.6 dBFS. The hand-off is the one stand-in that wanders (a row of one sample is a row of cards, not a machine).
